# goncordia

> Background job queue for Go that stores jobs in the database you already use (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DynamoDB, Firestore, in-memory). Transactional enqueue (outbox pattern), typed futures that await a job's result, retries, cron, retention by default, crash recovery, an embeddable admin UI, OpenTelemetry, and deterministic injected clocks.

Install: `go get github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/v2` plus one driver module, e.g. `github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/driver/pgxv5/v2`. Import paths carry `/v2`.

## Key concept

`EnqueueTx` enqueues a job inside your existing database transaction. The job becomes visible to workers only if the transaction commits — no dual-write risk, no relay process needed.

```go
tx, _ := pool.Begin(ctx)
queries.CreateOrder(ctx, tx, order)
client.EnqueueTx(ctx, tx, SendConfirmationArgs{OrderID: order.ID}, nil)
tx.Commit(ctx)  // job and order appear atomically
```

## Futures

Declare `future.Define[Args, Result]()` once; workers `Register` a handler, application code calls the bound `Func` without type parameters. Works on every backend; in-process waiters wake instantly, others poll.

```go
var Sum = future.Define[SumArgs, int]()
Sum.Register(registry, m, sumHandler, core.WorkerOpts{})
sum := future.Bind(m, client, Sum)
total, err := sum.Call(ctx, SumArgs{A: 2, B: 3}) // deletes its job after returning a value
```

## Retention

Worker pools prune by default on every driver, under a shared leader lease: completed and cancelled jobs after 24h, discarded after 7 days, future results after 1h. Tune with `WorkerConfig.Retention` (`goncordia.KeepForever` keeps a state) or disable with a negative `RetentionInterval`.

## MCP server

`github.com/kirimatt/goncordia/mcpserver/v2` lets AI agents inspect and operate the queue over MCP: `mcpserver.New(d)` serves read-only `list_queues`, `list_jobs`, `get_job`, `get_metrics`; `mcpserver.WithWriteTools()` adds `retry_job`, `reschedule_job`, `cancel_job`, `delete_job`, `pause_queue`, `resume_queue`. Serve with `mcpserver.Handler(srv)` (Streamable HTTP, behind your auth) or `srv.Run(ctx, &mcp.StdioTransport{})`. Docs: https://goncordia.docs7.io/mcp

## Supported backends

Postgres (pgx v5, database/sql, gorm, bun), MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, Amazon DynamoDB, Cloud Firestore, in-memory.

Transactional inserts supported on: Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Firestore (not in-memory, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DynamoDB).

## Performance

`bench/compare` runs the same workloads against River (Postgres) and Asynq and Machinery (Redis) on the same servers. Postgres: on par with River at a 1 ms fetch cooldown (draining 20,000 jobs: 5,801 vs 4,726 jobs/s with 10 workers, 20,610 vs 22,588 with 100), 2.8 ms idle pickup. Redis: drains 4–9× faster than Asynq and Machinery, 0.7 ms idle pickup. Tables: https://goncordia.docs7.io/benchmarks
